title: Model outage simulation & customer impact playbook
creator: Maya Patel
description: Objective: produce a reproducible simulation and playbook that quantifies customer-visible impact (latency, error rate, cost) for realistic model outage scenarios and prescribes prioritized mitigations for PLG and enterprise customers. Deliverables: simulation harness, cohort-level impact report, runbook templates (support + sales), example dashboard panels, and A/B test plan for fallback policy changes.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible simulation harness that can model at least 3 outage profiles (short spike, regional degradation, full-model unavailability) against production-like traffic
Cohort-level impact report showing latency, error surface, token-cost delta, and estimated ARR risk for top 20 customers
A runbook with step-by-step mitigation actions and automated rollback triggers integrated with Console alerting
A set of recommended fallback policies (model variant mappings, routing priorities, degrade-to-cached-response) with cost/latency tradeoffs quantified
Documentation and example dashboards (Grafana/Console) linked in Confluence and a handoff doc for Sales/CS
tasks: Design outage profiles and traffic replay methodology (PM + Eng)
Build a traffic replay + fault injector in staging that can emulate prefix cache warmup effects
Instrument telemetry to capture cohort-level KPIs (P95 latency, failed requests, token delta, cost delta)
Run simulation across 6 model variants and 4 region topologies, export datasets
Analyze results and produce per-cohort impact slices (SMB, mid-market, enterprise)
Draft runbook and escalation flow; review with Support and SRE
Publish Confluence playbook, add example panels to Console, and prepare a short internal demo
notes: We want to capture secondary effects: cache cold-start amplification, burst autoscaling delays, and cross-model KV cache compatibility issues
Simulations should be seeded with real customer traffic distributions (anonymized) where possible — ENG to provide sample traces
Priority cohorts: top 25 revenue customers, customers with strict latency SLAs, and PLG heavy users where perception matters
Consider a synthetic RAG workload to represent high-recall retrieval scenarios where latency amplifies user-visible degradation
recent_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with SRE + Support. Agreement on three canonical outage profiles (1m spike, 30m regional slowdown, region-wide model substitution). Action: ENG to provide trace sampler.
2026-03-06: ENG provided anonymized traffic sample for two enterprise customers and one PLG cohort. PM built initial cohort definitions.
2026-03-09: Prototype fault injector landed in staging (ENG-4111). First smoke runs show cache warmup dominates short spike scenario — needs separate analysis path.
2026-03-12: Draft runbook skeleton circulated. Support requested clearer rollback criteria — added as AC to acceptance_criteria. Next: schedule review with CS on 2026-03-18.
success_metrics: Simulation coverage: >=95% of traffic shape variance across seeded cohorts
Actionability: top-3 mitigations reduce customer-visible failed requests by >=60% in simulation
Time-to-mitigate: runbook steps reproducible within 15 minutes by Support engineer in tabletop
Business impact clarity: estimated ARR exposure per outage scenario for top 20 customers with +/-15% confidence
mitigation_plan: Tiered mitigations: 1) Automatic route to compatible model variants (fastest, lowest-friction) with token-cost guardrails; 2) Prefix/KV cache priming for hot cohorts; 3) Temporary rate-limit relaxations for enterprise flows with contractual protections; 4) Communication templates and sales playbook for enterprise engagement. Each mitigation must include telemetry hooks and a rollback path documented in Console alerts.
